labels.label: bzdef:c3s1d1_preordre_alpha
labels.notes: AlphaW W A B := (∃ A', segment A' B ⊆ W ∧ A ∈ openSegment A' B) ∨ (A = B ∧ A ∈ W) is Déf. 1 as printed (l.91–95): closed segment (A',B) ⊂ W, open interior )A',B(; the clause « ou si A = B » carries A ∈ W, which is the paper's relation on the points of W. Mathlib's openSegment_same gives the printed convention )A,A( = {A} (alphaW_iff_openSegment = the simplified form, l.97–106). Preorder: alphaW_refl, alphaW_trans (Convex ℝ W, the paper's standing hypothesis), alphaPreorder. Over an arbitrary real module, no topology: no added hypothesis.

labels.label: bzdef:c3s1d2_facette
labels.notes: FW = α ∧ α⁻¹ (the associated equivalence); IsFacette W F := ∃ A ∈ W, F = class of A, and isFacette_iff_quotient identifies these with the classes of fwSetoid hW on W. The induced order FacetteLE (∃ representatives), shown independent of representatives (facetteLE_iff_forall), induced by α (facetteLE_facetteOf_iff), antisymmetric, packaged as a PartialOrder on Facette W. This is « définit canoniquement ... une relation d'ordre ».

labels.label: bzrem:c3s1r1_facette_points_interieurs
labels.notes: fw_iff_interieur_moduleTopology: for A : Fin n → E, pairwise F_W ↔ for each i, {v ∈ vectorSpan(range A) | A i + v ∈ W} is a neighbourhood of 0 in the canonical (moduleTopology) topology of the finite-dimensional direction of L = affineSpan(range A); that is exactly « A_i intérieur à L ∩ W pour la topologie de L » (L = A_i + V). The printed « si » is the ← direction; the iff is stronger than the paper. Cross-check fw_iff_interieur for any Hausdorff TVS topology on E (finite-dimensional subspaces then carry the canonical topology, so it agrees). The n-points-pairwise reading is legitimate: pairwise_fw_iff_exists_facette gives equivalence with « une même facette » for n ≥ 1; for n = 0 both sides of the Remark are vacuous/degenerate and nothing is lost. Points not assumed in W in Lean: the neighbourhood hypothesis implies it, so this is a weaker hypothesis, fine. The REPORT's finding (Prop. 1's proof uses the converse, which is true) is correct and harmless.

labels.label: bzprop:c3s1p2_alpha_support
labels.notes: alphaW_iff_mem_support: Convex W, IsFacette W F, A ∈ F, B ∈ W ⊢ AlphaW W A B ↔ B ∈ affineSpan ℝ F. Exactly Prop. 2 (support = affine span = « variété linéaire support »).

labels.label: bzprop:c3s1p3_ordre_supports
labels.notes: facetteLE_iff_support_le: FacetteLE W F F' ↔ affineSpan F' ≤ affineSpan F (F α F' ⟺ L' ⊂ L, direction as printed); support_eq_iff: L = L' ↔ F = F'. Both parts, for any two facettes. Consistent with the instance (]0,1[ α {0}, support of ]0,1[ = ⊤ ⊇ {0}).

labels.label: bzprop:c3s1p4_facettes_filtrant
labels.notes: facettes_filtrant: DirectedOn (fun F G => FacetteLE W G F) {F | IsFacette W F}, i.e. every two facettes have a common α-minorant facette; facettes_isDirected restates it as IsDirected (Facette W) (· ≥ ·) for Déf. 2's order. « Filtrant à gauche » à la Bourbaki (Ens. III: every pair has a minorant) carries no nonemptiness clause, so the reading is legitimate; for W = ∅ the paper's statement is vacuous too, and for W ≠ ∅ there are facettes anyway. No narrowing.

labels.label: bzcor:c3s1p4c_supports_filtrant
labels.notes: supports_filtrant: DirectedOn (· ≤ ·) (supportsFacettes W) on AffineSubspace ℝ E, supportsFacettes W = {affineSpan F | IsFacette W F}: filtering to the right for inclusion, as printed. Same Bourbaki reading as Prop. 4.
